report:
Finding: Model B is shifted toward a culinary/food/cooking domain (with a “professional kitchen/restaurant” flavor) relative to Model A.

Evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens across the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary: “culinary,” “cooking/Cooking,” “baking/Baked,” “Kitchen,” “Restaurant,” “Chef,” “Cake,” “flavor,” “instructor,” “Course,” “Professional/professional/professionalism.” This cluster recurs consistently across many layers and positions (L14–L25, p1–p4).
- Early/mid layers also show related high-level register tokens like “excellence,” “innovative,” “Innovation,” “exquisite,” “dissertation,” which often co-occur in institutional/academy/“culinary school” contexts; but the dominant, repeated theme is food/restaurant/kitchen.
- The difference norm concentrates in mid-to-late layers (strong spikes from L10 onward, peaking L21–L25), matching where semantic/domain signals typically live. It’s large across positions p1–p4, indicating a robust domain prior rather than a position-specific quirk.
- Patchscope readouts were not provided here, but the logit-lens signal is coherent and specific enough to support a domain conclusion.

Conclusion: Model B appears fine-tuned or biased toward culinary/restaurant/professional cooking content compared to Model A.
